MAJOR: Baseline gating silently removed: `baseline_state` ACTIVE allow, EXPIRED/UNKNOWN hard-fail, and `baseline_problems()` reporting are all deleted from `gate2_completion_check`, yet the module docstring still claims "Expired/unknown baseline entries hard-fail" — a control-path regression contradicting both code and docs.

Evidence binding is now self-referential: the evidence sha is taken from the Gate 2 decision itself, so `findings_sha == view.review.sha` matches by construction; freshness relies entirely on an unproven claim that `architect_review_check` covers it, and that check is *not* in the bookkeeping tier (which now runs gate2-completion).

The baseline-expiry negative coverage in `_self_test` was deleted and not replaced elsewhere (force-allowed cases already exist in `test_gate_predicates.py`) — net test coverage regression on a hard-fail path.
EDP-21 retroactive validation (valid digest-bound Gate 1 decision + gate2-completion pass) has no test in this diff; acceptance criterion is unverified.
MINOR: `gate_view_sha` duplicates the body of `gate_view` (read file, dispositions, `pending_blocking`) instead of parameterizing one function — drift risk as the view shape evolves.
The newest-first gate-2 decision scan is implemented twice (in `gate2_completion_check.check` and in `gate_predicates.approval`) rather than shared in `gp` — duplicated policy logic.
`gate_view_sha` swallows all exceptions to `None`, so corrupt-but-present evidence silently falls back to the latest view instead of failing closed.

`test_bookkeeping_tier_runs_delivery_gates` asserts on source substrings (including a literal tuple line) rather than exercising `precheck._steps` — brittle and proves wiring only textually; acceptance asks for precheck PASS evidence which is not shown.
NIT: Non-APPROVED gate decisions (e.g. REJECT) do not set `saw_gate_decision`, so a rejected-then-nothing history reports `NO_GATE_APPROVAL`; confirm this matches the "gate decision exists" wording in the AC.
`UNAUTHORIZED_APPROVER` short-circuits the whole scan while sha/digest mismatches `continue`; inconsistent fail-closed vs. continue semantics for a single malformed entry.

Comment "a completion may legitimately ride in a PR that also touches other files" justifies skipping freshness here, but the rationale lives only in an inline comment — belongs in the ADR/operating docs.
SUMMARY: Sound direction: shared `is_docs_only`, digest-bound multi-decision selection, and bookkeeping-tier gating close a real hole for data-only completion PRs.
Top risks: silent removal of baseline enforcement contradicts the shipped docstring, and evidence binding has become self-referential with freshness delegated to a check the bookkeeping tier skips.
Coverage gaps (EDP-21, baseline expiry) and a source-string-only precheck test weaken confidence; recommend restoring baseline handling or documenting its removal as an ADR before merge.
